source_row.rationale: Per ADA diagnostic criteria, an HbA1c of 6.5% or higher (confirmed on two separate testing occasions, unless there is unequivocal hyperglycemia with classic symptoms) is used to diagnose diabetes mellitus, reflecting average blood glucose control over approximately the preceding 2-3 months. An HbA1c of 5.7%-6.4% generally indicates prediabetes, while below 5.7% is considered normal.
source_row.source_name: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care, HbA1c Diagnostic Criteria
